title: Near-IR Observations of the Young Star [BHB2007]-1: A Substellar Companion Opening the Gap in the Disk
question: Investigate whether a planet or brown dwarf companion is carving the dust gap in the protoplanetary disk around [BHB2007]-1 using new VLT/NACO NIR observations.

what.value: ALMA continuum and CO maps, stellar coordinates, disk inclination (75 deg), disk PA (12.5 deg), mm cavity size (~70 au), dynamical stellar mass (2.23 M_sun), systemic velocity (3.6 km/s), and VLA 14-mm map

evidence.quote: For the astrometric calibration, we adopted the ALMA coordinates for the center of the star, RA=17:11:03.9234 and Dec=-27:22:55.4725, as measured in (cite: Alves2020).
Here, we assume that the midplane is given by the disk PA of 12.5$^\circ$, as determined from the ALMA continuum by (cite: Alves2020).
The height profile is then deprojected by the disk inclination by dividing by $\sin(i)$, where $i=75^\circ$ as reported in (cite: Alves2020).

what.value: Effective temperatures T_eff = 4060 K for [BHB2007]-1 and T_eff = 3346 K for [BHB2007]-2, and JHK spectra

evidence.quote: with the effective temperature constrained by (cite: Covey2010) ($T_{\rm eff}=4060$ K and $T_{\rm eff}=3346$ K, for -1 and -2, respectively, with typical uncertainties of $\pm$300 K)

recipe.goal: Reduce VLT/NACO NIR data and subtract stellar PSF
recipe.method: Background subtraction (one frame from median of others), flat-fielding, recentering, median combination; 2D elliptical Gaussian fit to center, azimuthal average over angles devoid of emission (PA 230 to 350 deg) expanded to 2D PSF and subtracted
key_parameters: Azimuthal average angles: PA 230 deg to 350 deg

recipe.goal: Assess astrometry, distance, and physical association of sources in field
recipe.method: Query Gaia EDR3 astrometric fidelity classifier and compare relative astrometry across two NACO epochs (~4 years apart)
assumptions: Distance of 166 pc adopted for [BHB2007]-1 from [BHB2007]-2 Gaia EDR3 parallax

recipe.goal: Derive stellar properties (visual extinction, luminosity, mass, and age)
recipe.method: Fit B-to-W4 photometry with Phoenix stellar photosphere models to obtain A_V and L_*, then compare with pre-main-sequence evolutionary tracks

recipe.goal: Measure NIR disk brightness contrast and vertical scattering surface height profile
recipe.method: Compute disk-to-stellar light contrast phi = F_disk * 4*pi*r^2 / F_*; trace disk surface by fitting a Gaussian as a function of height along disk PA, deproject by sin(i), and fit power-law h(R) ~ R^(1+alpha)
assumptions: Disk midplane PA = 12.5 deg and inclination i = 75 deg from ALMA continuum

recipe.goal: Characterize position and mass of embedded substellar companion candidate
recipe.method: Measure position and L' flux ratio on PSF-subtracted image and compare with COND, DUSTY, and BEX evolutionary models
assumptions: System age of 0.9-5.7 Myr, primary star L' magnitude of 7.93 (from WISE W1), and distance of 166 pc

score_reason: Archival ESO/ALMA/VLA program IDs are clearly given and the analytical steps (azimuthal PSF subtraction, contrast calculation, Gaussian vertical profile fitting, and evolutionary model comparison) are conceptually well described, but no software tools, scripts, or exact photometric extraction parameters are specified.
rediscovery_reason: The raw VLT/NACO and ALMA data are public in the ESO and ALMA archives, the custom azimuthal PSF subtraction method is straightforward to implement from the text description, and the main results (companion L' flux ratio, position, and disk North/South contrast ratios) are concrete numeric values.
